Title: Who is playing, and where are they when they play?
Detail_lesson: Kids on a bus, a team at a party, one person on a lunch break. It changes everything.
ClaudeNote: Design the controls, the length of a round and the look for the winning answer.

Title: What should a player feel in the first minute?
Detail_lesson: Curious, rushed, clever, scared, silly. Pick the feeling, then build for it.
ClaudeNote: Make every choice in the first minute serve the winning feeling. Say how.

Title: Why would someone play a second time?
Detail_lesson: A better score, a new level, a friend to beat, a different ending.
ClaudeNote: Build the winning reason into the end of a round: show it before the player leaves.

Title: What does the player do in the first ten seconds?
Detail_lesson: Tap, jump, sort, guess, steer. The one action the whole game is built on.
CustomInstruction: A verb and what it does.
Placeholder: A verb and what it does.
ClaudeNote: This is the core action. Build it first, playable, before anything else, and post when it works.

Title: How does a player win, and how do they lose?
Detail_lesson: If nobody can say it in one line each, the game is not ready yet.
CustomInstruction: One line to win, one line to lose.
Placeholder: One line to win, one line to lose.
ClaudeNote: Make the winning answers the rules. Show each on the screen in one line.

Title: What is the one rule that makes this game different?
Detail_lesson: Every game is like another one. What is the twist that makes this one ours?
ClaudeNote: Treat the winning rule as the heart of the game; never cut it to save time.

Title: How long is one round?
Detail_lesson: Think of where people will play it.
Options: Under a minute|About three minutes|Ten minutes or more
ClaudeNote: Size every round to the winning length.

Title: Should there be a timer on the screen?
Detail_lesson: A clock adds pressure. Some games need it, some do not.
ClaudeNote: If most say yes, show the time left in every round. If no, keep rounds untimed.

Title: Which game is this like, and what would we change?
Detail_lesson: Snake, but you shrink. Tetris, but the pieces are words.
CustomInstruction: Name the game and the change.
Placeholder: Name the game and the change.
ClaudeNote: Say what you would borrow from the winning game and what you would change, in a few lines.

Title: How would this work as a board game or a playground game?
Detail_lesson: Take away the screen. What is left is the fun part.
ClaudeNote: Say which part of the winning answer the build should keep, and what it would replace.

Title: What if the players worked together instead of against each other?
Detail_lesson: Many good games are about a team beating the game, not each other.
CustomInstruction: How would that change the game?
Placeholder: How would that change the game?
ClaudeNote: Say what the winning idea would take to build next to the current game. Do not switch unless a Do now says so.

Title: Who should the player play against?
Detail_lesson: It changes what the game is about.
Options: The game itself|A friend on the same screen|Their own best score
ClaudeNote: Say what the winning choice would take to build next to the current game. Do not switch unless a Do now says so.

Title: What was confusing in the first try?
Detail_lesson: Watch someone play for the first time. Where did they stop?
ClaudeNote: Fix the top answer first, usually with a hint on the screen, not more rules.

Title: When did it get boring?
Detail_lesson: Too slow, too easy, too much the same. Find the moment.
ClaudeNote: Change the pacing at the winning moment: add a twist, speed it up or shorten it. Say what you changed.

Title: What would make it fairer?
Detail_lesson: A player should lose because of what they did, not because of luck or a bug.
ClaudeNote: Fix the top answer and say what you changed.

Title: How hard is it?
Detail_lesson: For the people it is for.
ClaudeNote: Move the difficulty toward About right. Say what you changed.

Title: Can a new player start without reading any rules?
Detail_lesson: Watch someone pick it up for the first time.
ClaudeNote: If most say no, replace the rules with a hint on the screen at the moment it is needed.

Title: How fun is it so far?
Detail_lesson: Play a round, then rate it.
ClaudeNote: If the average is under 4, fix the reason given most often before adding anything.

Title: What should the next level add?
Detail_lesson: A new obstacle, a new power, a new place. One thing.
ClaudeNote: Put the winning answers on the Later list as the next levels.

Title: What would make you share this with a friend?
Detail_lesson: A score to beat, a funny moment, a picture of the ending.
ClaudeNote: Add the winning answers to the Later list, and say which is the smallest to build.

Title: Is the first level ready for people to play?
Detail_lesson: Ready means someone new could play it start to finish.
ClaudeNote: If most say no, fix what they name before adding a level.

Title: Would you play it again tomorrow?
Detail_lesson: Honestly, for real, tomorrow.
ClaudeNote: Put this score and its top reason in the wrap-up summary.
